subtitle: Fire in Words, Stone in Memory

panels.shot: epic triptych wide, figures emerging against temple towers and open sky
panels.action: Basavanna stands in a bustling Kalyana street, Akka Mahadevi walks bare-shouldered into wild forest, and Harihara writes in a Halebidu hall where sculpted Hoysalas loom around him.

dialogue.text: In twelfth‑century Karnataka, Basavanna, Akka Mahadevi and Harihara turned temple stone into moving words that still ask: where does the true shrine of courage and devotion really stand?

i18n.hi: बारहवीं सदी के कर्नाटक में बसवन्ना, अक्का महादेवी और हरिहरा ने मंदिर की पत्थर दीवारों को चलते शब्दों में बदल दिया, जो आज भी पूछते हैं: साहस और भक्ति का असली देवस्थान कहाँ है?

panels.shot: slow push-in on Basavanna and Akka in dim interior, Harihara faintly superimposed like a future echo
panels.action: Basavanna leans over a palm‑leaf manuscript by a lamp, Akka Mahadevi’s profile appears in the shadowed doorway, while a ghostly image of Harihara writing hovers like memory behind them.

dialogue.text: The record preserves their words, not their faces. Vachanas burn on palm leaf, and Harihara’s ragales turn those brief flames into long, flowing memory.

i18n.hi: दस्तावेज़ उनके शब्द बचाते हैं, चेहरे नहीं। वचन ताड़–पत्रों पर जलते हैं, और हरिहरा की रगले उन छोटी लौओं को लंबी, बहती याद में बदल देती हैं।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye over Kalyana, showing palace, crowded streets, shrines and craft quarters
panels.action: From high above Kalyana, dusty streets teem with traders and priests below the Kalachuri stronghold, while somewhere in the maze Basavanna walks among smiths and workers with his small group of sharanas.

dialogue.text: Kalyana, under the Kalachuris, is full of shrines, markets and rank. Basavanna’s vachanas rise here, challenging caste, ritual and power in everyday Kannada.

i18n.hi: कलचुरियों के अधीन कल्याण: मंदिरों, बाज़ारों और ऊँच–नीच से भरा शहर। यही से बसवन्ना के वचन उठते हैं, रोज़मर्रा की कन्नड में जाति, कर्मकांड और सत्ता को ललकारते हुए।

panels.shot: low-angle street scene focused on Basavanna among diverse townsfolk
panels.action: Basavanna stands in a small street circle speaking to cobblers, brahmins, women and labourers, his hand resting on the ishtalinga at his chest, as a distant temple gopura looms.

dialogue.text: His poems say: the lord of Kudalasangama cares little for birth or badge. He points to the linga worn on the body, the labour of hands, the honesty of speech.

i18n.hi: उसकी कविताएँ कहती हैं: कुदालसंगम का देव जन्म या पद से नहीं, देह पर पहनी लिंग से, हाथों की मेहनत से और बोले गए सच्चे शब्द से ख़ुश होता है।

panels.shot: intimate medium shot of Basavanna reciting, listeners intent
panels.action: Basavanna recites a vachana in a modest hall; some men in sacred thread listen uneasily while a leather‑worker and a woman sit forward, eyes alight.

dialogue.speaker: akka_mahadevi_basavanna_and_harihara
dialogue.text: “The rich build tall temples. I build one with my body, Kudalasangama Deva.”

i18n.hi: “अमीर ऊँचे मंदिर बनाते हैं। मैं अपने शरीर को ही मंदिर बनाता हूँ, कुदालसंगम देवा।”

panels.shot: cross-fade style composition, showing traditional temple rites on one side, simple personal worship on the other
panels.action: On one side priests perform elaborate rites before a stone linga; on the other a farmer in a field touches his small personal linga, eyes closed in quiet devotion.

dialogue.text: Vachanas do not erase temples. They shift the centre. They ask: is God trapped in stone and ritual, or walking with the work‑worn, inside each living body?

i18n.hi: वचन मंदिरों को मिटाते नहीं, बस धुरी बदल देते हैं। सवाल उठाते हैं: क्या ईश्वर पत्थर और कर्मकांड में कैद है, या मेहनतकशों के साथ चलता है, हर देह के भीतर?

panels.shot: medium shot in a simple gathering, suggesting but not over-defining the Anubhava Mantapa
panels.action: Basavanna sits with Allama Prabhu and other sharanas in a plain hall, no throne or banner, words passing between them like a quiet current.

dialogue.text: Later tradition calls it Anubhava Mantapa, a hall of experience. The evidence shows circles of debate and shared poems, not minutes of a formal council.

i18n.hi: बाद की परंपरा इसे अनुभव मंटपा कहती है, अनुभव का मंडप। साक्ष्य बताते हैं यहाँ बहस के गोले और साझा कविताएँ थीं, न कि किसी औपचारिक परिषद की कार्यवाही।

panels.shot: dramatic doorway shot as Akka enters the gathering, everyone turning
panels.action: Akka Mahadevi steps into the hall, her body draped only in long, flowing hair, head high, as startled men rise and one older sharana gestures for calm.

dialogue.text: Into this male world walks Akka Mahadevi. Her vachanas say: “What use are silks? Cover me, O Lord, with your grace alone.” The shock is social, the resolve fierce.

i18n.hi: इसी पुरुष–प्रधान दुनिया में अक्का महादेवी कदम रखती है। उसके वचन कहते हैं: “रेशम से क्या हासिल? प्रभु, मुझे बस अपनी कृपा से ढँक दो।” समाज हिलता है, उसका संकल्प तेज़ है।

panels.shot: close-up on Akka’s face, forest backdrop, suggesting her later wandering
panels.action: Akka Mahadevi walks alone through thick forest, leaves glistening with rain, her eyes focused, mouth slightly parted as if murmuring a vachana to Chennamallikarjuna.

dialogue.speaker: akka_mahadevi_basavanna_and_harihara
dialogue.text: “Husbands and kings are passing clouds. You alone, white jasmine Lord, are mine.”

i18n.hi: “पति–राजा तो चलते बादल हैं। तुम ही हो, सफेद मल्लिगे के स्वामी, जो मेरे हो।”

panels.shot: montage-style wide shot: Brahmin ritual, caste markers, then Basava and Akka speaking against them
panels.action: A brahmin instructs a man to stand apart due to caste; in the same frame Basavanna speaks to both, while Akka turns away from ornaments laid out for her.

dialogue.text: Caste lines, gender codes, ritual demands: the vachanas cut across all three. They make devotion a direct bond, not a contract mediated by rank and rule.

i18n.hi: जाति की रेखाएँ, लिंग के नियम, पूजा की माँगें—वचन इन तीनों को चीर देते हैं। भक्ति को सीधा रिश्ता बना देते हैं, न कि दर्जे और हुक्म से चला सौदा।

panels.shot: shadowed palace corridor contrasting with open street gathering
panels.action: In a dim corridor, Kalachuri officials confer with guards, while outside Basavanna’s mixed‑caste followers share food in the street, some nobles watching with tight jaws.

dialogue.text: Power watches. For some, equality feels like revolt. Later stories turn Basava into a royal minister, but records keep him closer to reformer than court pillar.

i18n.hi: सत्ता देख रही है। कईयों को बराबरी बगावत लगती है। आगे की कहानियाँ बसवन्ना को राज–मंत्री बनाती हैं, पर लिखित सबूत उसे दरबार के स्तंभ से ज़्यादा सुधारक दिखाते हैं।

panels.shot: tense medium shot at a marriage feast between castes
panels.action: A wedding between a brahmin woman and a lower‑caste sharana takes place in a courtyard; garlands hang, but onlookers are split between joy and anger, one official turning away.

dialogue.text: Marriages across caste, shared meals, outspoken poems: such acts deepen strain. The movement faces backlash, and Kalyana’s world grows more dangerous for its boldest voices.

i18n.hi: जाति से परे विवाह, साथ बैठकर भोजन, खुलकर लिखी कविताएँ—ऐसे काम टकराव बढ़ाते हैं। आंदोलन पर चोट पड़ती है और कल्याण की हवा उसके सबसे निडर स्वरों के लिए ख़तरनाक होती जाती है।

panels.shot: transition shot: map-like vista from Kalyana to Halebidu with travel path
panels.action: A stylised landscape shows Kalyana fading in the north as the scene shifts southward toward Halebidu’s rising temples, a thin trail linking the two.

dialogue.text: Yet the poems move. From Kalyana, vachanas travel by memory and palm leaf into other Kannada lands, where another kind of temple is rising in stone.

i18n.hi: फिर भी कविताएँ चलती रहती हैं। कल्याण से वचन यादों और ताड़–पत्रों पर चढ़कर दूसरे कन्नड इलाकों में पहुँचते हैं, जहाँ पत्थर से एक और तरह का मंदिर उठ रहा है।

panels.shot: majestic wide shot of Halebidu temple exterior under clear sky
panels.action: The Hoysala temple at Halebidu rises like a carved mountain, walls crowded with dancers, deities and warriors, under a bright Karnataka sky.

dialogue.text: Halebidu, heart of the Hoysalas. Here stone is grammar: every curve and frieze speaks of gods, kings and battles. Into this world steps the poet Harihara.

i18n.hi: हलेबीडु, होयसलों का दिल। यहाँ पत्थर ही व्याकरण है: हर मोड़ और पट्टी देवों, राजाओं और युद्धों की बोली बोलती है। इसी दुनिया में कवि हरिहरा कदम रखता है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Harihara inside temple hall, looking at carvings, then down to his manuscript
panels.action: Harihara stands in a shadowed mandapa, fingers tracing a sculpted panel, then sits to write on palm leaf, the temple columns receding behind him.

dialogue.text: Harihara hears of Basavanna’s fire and chooses a different tool: the ragale, a flowing Kannada verse that can carry biography, devotion and moral reflection together.

i18n.hi: हरिहरा बसवन्ना की आग सुनता है और दूसरा औज़ार चुनता है: रगले, बहती कन्नड छंद जो जीवनी, भक्ति और नैतिक सोच को साथ–साथ ढो सकती है।

panels.shot: close-up on Harihara’s determined face, faint images of Basava and Akka in thought-cloud style around
panels.action: Harihara writes intently, as faint imagined figures of Basavanna among workers and Akka in the forest flicker around him like remembered scenes.

dialogue.text: His Basavarajadevara Ragale is one of the earliest lives of Basava we have. It shapes how later ages remember the man behind the vachanas and the world that resisted him.

i18n.hi: उसकी ‘बसवराजदेवर रगले’ बसवन्ना की सबसे शुरुआती जीवन कथाओं में से एक है। यही बाद के युगों को सिखाती है कि वचनों के पीछे का आदमी और उसे रोकती दुनिया कैसी थी।

panels.shot: medium shot: Harihara reading aloud to a small group in Halebidu
panels.action: Harihara sits amid courtiers, sculptors and townsfolk, reciting from his ragale; some nod, others listen in careful stillness as temple bells hang in the background.

dialogue.speaker: akka_mahadevi_basavanna_and_harihara
dialogue.text: “Basava, servant of Kudalasangama, walked against the river of custom.”

i18n.hi: “बसवा, कुदालसंगम का सेवक, रिवाज़ों की धारा के उलट चला।”

panels.shot: split composition: on one side a sculptor carving, on the other a scribe copying vachanas
panels.action: A Hoysala sculptor hammers delicately at a stone figure; nearby, a scribe copies vachanas onto fresh palm leaves, both bathed in the same shaft of light.

dialogue.text: Thus two temples grow. One in stone, set in a capital; another in words, carried by singers and scribes into homes, workshops and wandering minds.

i18n.hi: यूँ दो मंदिर उगते हैं। एक पत्थर का, राजधानी में गड़ा हुआ; दूसरा शब्दों का, गायक–लेखक उठाकर घरों, कारखानों और भटकती सोचों तक ले जाते हैं।

panels.shot: conceptual overhead shot showing waves of time: Kalyana, Halebidu, modern readers
panels.action: From above, Kalyana’s streets and Halebidu’s temples blur into a flowing timeline that ends with a modern reader holding a book of vachanas under a bare tree.

dialogue.text: Today, debates about sect and founder continue, but the vachanas still ask each listener the same hard question: will you build your temple in stone, or in the courage to live truthfully?

i18n.hi: आज भी पंथ और संस्थापक पर बहस जारी है, पर वचन हर सुनने वाले से वही कड़ा सवाल पूछते हैं: तुम अपना मंदिर पत्थर में बनाओगे, या सच्चा जीने के साहस में?

subtitle_i18n.en: Fire in Words, Stone in Memory
subtitle_i18n.hi: शब्दों में आग, यादों में पत्थर
